seed_edits.reason: Corrected placement of Hubert's qualifying thumbsup reaction: moved from an unrelated #general message (a channel Hubert is not even a member of) onto johndoe's SSO-login teammate post inside #engineering itself. This makes 'the channel where Hubert Marek is a member and has reacted with a thumbsup to a teammate's post' resolve to the same channel for both facts, per the ordinary reading of the prompt, while still keeping the reaction off the reply-target message itself as the design's binding note requires.

Negative alternative: a thumbsup reaction exists in #random from Kenji, who holds no channel_members row for #engineering, illustrating that a reactor lacking membership in the qualifying channel cannot stand in for Hubert Marek.

notes: Repaired the validity defect: the focal query alone (matching the assigned route order MESSAGE->CONVERSATION->CONVERSATION_MEMBERSHIP->USER->REACTION) still cannot itself tie the reaction's message to the root message's channel, since REACTION is only adjacent to USER. The auxiliary query now supplies that missing same-channel constraint directly off the root's own channel_id (messages.channel_id -> channels -> messages.channel_id -> message_reactions.message_id -> message_reactions.user_id), requiring that Hubert's thumbsup sit on some message inside the SAME channel as the candidate root message, without hardcoding any channel ID. To make this satisfiable at all, Hubert's qualifying reaction was relocated (via seed edit) from an unrelated #general message he isn't even a member of, onto johndoe's SSO-login post inside #engineering itself -- still a different message from the crash-report reply target, honoring the design's binding note that the reaction need not be on the reply target, while now genuinely sharing the channel that both the membership and reaction facts jointly identify, matching the prompt's ordinary-language reading. Focal+auxiliary together yield the single correct match 1699824000.000987; the two message-content negatives remain excluded by the crash-report/rate-limit filters, and Kenji's out-of-channel reaction and Morgan's reaction-less membership remain as supporting non-qualifying records illustrating the membership and reaction boundary, per the design's fixed negative roles. Discovery still relies only on conversations.list, conversations.members, conversations.history, reactions.get, and chat.postMessage; the access plan can now be understood as scanning reactions within Hubert's own member channels rather than an unbounded workspace-wide search.
